review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its simp lemmas are used, in the file and elsewhere in Mathlib (Injective.lean, HahnEmbedding.lean, VectorSpace.lean). The `neg`, `zero`, `smul` and `vadd` families are simp-tagged consistently. `smul_apply` is covered by `coe_smul` plus `Pi.smul_apply`, so I did not flag it. I considered tagging `map_add`, `map_sub` and `map_smul` as simp but did not report it. Several downstream uses rewrite them right-to-left (`simp_rw [← ….map_add]`), so a simp tag could interfere. I did not run Lean, so the proposed tags and their effect on the in-file proofs are untested.

findings.excerpt: theorem add_domain (f g : E →ₛₗ.[σ] F) : (f + g).domain = f.domain ⊓ g.domain := rfl
findings.problem: The `Add` and `Sub` structure lemmas are not simp, although the parallel `zero_domain`, `zero_apply`, `neg_domain`, `neg_apply`, `smul_domain` and `vadd_domain` are. As a result `simp` cannot reduce `(f + g).domain` or `(f - g) x`, even though the normal form is clear (`f.domain ⊓ g.domain` and `f ⟨x, _⟩ - g ⟨x, _⟩`). Every proof about these operations in the file has to name the lemmas by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `add_domain`, `sub_domain`, `add_apply` and `sub_apply` with `@[simp]`, like their `neg` and `vadd` counterparts. The right-hand sides are strictly smaller or more primitive, so there is no cycle. Then drop the explicit lemma names from `simp [add_domain]` and `simp [add_apply]` in `instAddZeroClass`, `instAddSemigroup`, `instAddCommMonoid` and `instSubtractionCommMonoid` where that works, and keep `simp only` where it is intended.
findings.benefit: Downstream users get `simp` to unfold the domain and application of sums and differences of partial maps, consistently with negation, scalar action and vadd. The in-file proofs no longer repeat the same lemma names.

evidence.excerpt: theorem neg_domain (f : E →ₛₗ.[σ] F) : (-f).domain = f.domain := rfl
